raw_case_text:
The patient was a 21-year-old primigravida who was referred to the high-risk prenatal service of the Department of Obstetrics of the Federal University of Sao Paulo (UNIFESP) because of a finding of fetal ascites on morphological ultrasonography performed in the second trimester of pregnancy. In a routine prenatal serological test performed in a public healthcare clinic, VDRL 1/32 was detected in the 7th week of pregnancy. However, for socioeconomic reasons, the treatment for syphilis was only started in the 25th week of pregnancy, using benzathine penicillin (total dose of 7,200,000 UI). VDRL was 1/4 after this treatment. Morphological ultrasonography performed at another service in the second trimester detected a separate finding of fetal ascites. In the 31st week of pregnancy, when the woman was referred to UNIFESP's high-risk prenatal service, ultrasonography was performed again and the following fetal abnormalities were detected: voluminous ascites, splenomegaly, pericardial effusion, twisting of the toes, and hyperechogenicity of the cerebral parenchyma (Figures 1(a), 1(b), and 1(c)). In order to better assess the surface malformations, 3DUS was performed using the Voluson E8 apparatus (General Electric Medical Systems, Zipf, Austria), equipped with a volumetric convex transducer (RAB 4-8 L). The 3D imaging in rendering mode enabled clear assessment of the fetal limbs, especially the feet, which appeared twisted and lacked of some toes (Figure 1(d)). Three-dimensional imaging was of great importance in enabling the parents to understand the pathological condition better, and this allowed us to provide better counseling for prenatal care, obstetric management, and neonatal followup.
New serological tests for syphilis were performed in the 32nd week. VDRL was 1/64 and the specific treponemal test (ELISA-TPMA) was positive. The patient was then hospitalized for new treatment with benzathine penicillin (7,200,000 UI) and monitoring of fetal vitality. Cordocentesis performed in the 33rd week confirmed the diagnosis of fetal syphilis. Because of the many structural abnormalities presented by the fetus, it was decided to perform cesarean delivery at term. The newborn presented adequate vitality, weight of 3,095 g, and Apgar of 9/10 and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (ICU). In the ICU, the newborn underwent paracentesis and spinal tap, from which the specific treponemal test and VDRL were positive. Cytological tests on the fetal cerebrospinal fluid showed elevated cellularity. The newborn was kept in hospital for 14 days, receiving crystalline penicillin, and was then discharged without presenting any intercurrences.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 21-year-old primigravida was referred at 31 weeks' gestation for evaluation of severe fetal hydrops/ascites and congenital malformations following delayed prenatal treatment for maternal syphilis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Routine prenatal screening at 7 weeks' gestation detected a maternal serum VDRL of 1:32, but due to socioeconomic barriers, treatment with intramuscular benzathine penicillin (total dose 7,200,000 IU) was delayed until 25 weeks' gestation (after which maternal VDRL fell to 1:4). Second-trimester ultrasound detected fetal ascites, and repeat referral ultrasound at 31 weeks' gestation revealed progressive fetal ascites, splenomegaly, pericardial effusion, cerebral parenchymal hyperechogenicity, and distal limb deformities.
subjective.past_medical_history: 21-year-old primigravida with first-trimester maternal syphilis (VDRL 1:32 at 7 weeks' gestation) treated late at 25 weeks' gestation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Maternally asymptomatic; referred for abnormal second- and third-trimester fetal ultrasound findings.

objective.physical_examination: The term neonate was delivered via scheduled cesarean section weighing 3,095 g with Apgar scores of 9 and 10 and distal foot/toe deformities.
objective.routine_investigations: Maternal VDRL rose from 1:4 (post-25-week treatment) to 1:64 at 32 weeks' gestation with a positive treponemal ELISA-TPMA.
objective.advanced_workup: 2D and 3D obstetric ultrasound at 31 weeks' gestation demonstrated voluminous fetal ascites, splenomegaly, pericardial effusion, cerebral parenchymal hyperechogenicity, and twisted fetal feet with oligodactyly (missing toes). Cordocentesis at 33 weeks' gestation confirmed fetal congenital syphilis. Postnatal neonatal paracentesis and lumbar puncture in the NICU demonstrated elevated CSF cellularity (pleocytosis) and reactive fluid/CSF VDRL and specific treponemal tests.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed severe intrauterine and neonatal congenital syphilis with congenital neurosyphilis, fetal ascites, hepatosplenomegaly, pericardial effusion, and acral limb malformations due to delayed initial maternal treatment and maternal re-infection/relapse (maternal VDRL 1:64 at 32 weeks; confirmed by 33-week cordocentesis and postnatal neonatal paracentesis and CSF VDRL/treponemal positivity). The mother was re-treated inpatient at 32 weeks with benzathine penicillin G (total 7,200,000 IU), and following term cesarean delivery, the newborn was treated in the NICU with intravenous aqueous crystalline penicillin G for 14 days and discharged in stable condition.
